title: 2023 HMMT November Theme Problem 8
statement: Call a number feared if it contains the digits 13 as a contiguous substring and fearless otherwise. (For example, 132 is feared, while 123 is fearless.) Compute the smallest positive integer \(n\) such that there exists a positive integer \(a<100\) such that \(n\) and \(n+10 a\) are fearless while \(n+a, n+2 a, \ldots, n+9 a\) are all feared.

solutions.text:
First of all, note that we cannot have \(n, n+a, \ldots, n+10 a\) be less than 1000 , since we cannot have fearless numbers have 13 as their last two digits since \(a<100\), and \(129,130,131, \ldots, 139\) doesn't work as 139 is feared.
Thus, we must utilize numbers of the form \(13 x y\), where \(1,3, x\), and \(y\) are digits. If all of \(n+a, n+\) \(2 a, \ldots, n+9 a\) start with 13 , then \(a \leq 12\), and the minimum we can achieve is 1288 , with

\[1288,1300,1312, \ldots, 1384,1396,1408\]

If, however, \(n+9 a=1413\), then we can take \(a=14\) to get

\[1287,1301,1315, \ldots, 1399,1413,1427\]

so the minimum possible value is 1287 .
